sphl_manual.title: SPHL OPERATIONS MANUAL — PAGE 12
sphl_manual.body:
SELF-PROPELLED HYPERBARIC LIFEBOAT — OCCUPANT NOTICE

This vessel is a pressure chamber. If you are reading this, the automated decompression schedule is ACTIVE. Do not attempt to open the hatch before the surface-pressure indicator reads zero. Explosive decompression at depth-saturation is not survivable.

The schedule cannot be shortened. The schedule cannot be paused. Your body is being returned to the surface world at the only speed it will tolerate.

Remain calm. Ration water. The sea will hold you until the machine is done.

— Meridian Deep Energy, Marine Safety Division

pressure_log.title: AUTOMATED PRESSURE LOG
pressure_log.body:
DECOMPRESSION SCHEDULE — DAY 6 OF 6

DAY 1 — 09.2 BAR. OCCUPANT UNRESPONSIVE. VITALS STABLE.
DAY 2 — 07.4 BAR. OCCUPANT UNRESPONSIVE. VITALS STABLE.
DAY 3 — 05.1 BAR. OCCUPANT INTERMITTENTLY CONSCIOUS. SEDATION MAINTAINED PER PROTOCOL.
DAY 4 — 03.3 BAR. HULL CONTACT EVENT. DRIFT ANCHOR DEPLOYED.
DAY 5 — 01.9 BAR. OCCUPANT RESTLESS. SPOKE. NO CREW RESPONSE LOGGED.
DAY 6 — 01.0 BAR. SURFACE PRESSURE IMMINENT.

NOTE: NO RESPONSE FROM FIELD TRAFFIC CONTROL ON ANY CHANNEL. DAYS 1 THROUGH 6.

crew_letter_1.title: UNSENT LETTER — BUNKHOUSE CABIN 2
crew_letter_1.body:
Marta —

Three more weeks and I'm done, I mean it this time. The money's good but something's gone strange out here. They cut the food order again and nobody will say why. Whole pallets of tinned stuff going out on the supply boat instead of in.

Don't tell your mother I said this, but the water's wrong lately. Osk saw something off the derrick at night watch, wouldn't say what, and he doesn't spook.

Kiss the boys. Three weeks.

— Henrik

crew_letter_2.title: NOTE TAPED INSIDE A LOCKER — CABIN 5
crew_letter_2.body:
To whoever gets this bunk after me:

The heater rattles unless you wedge a coin in the grate. Third rung on the aft ladder is loose. Cook does real eggs on Sundays if you're early.

And do yourself a favor — don't ask about the rig at the end of the line. Not because you'll get in trouble. Because nobody knows anything, and watching them realize it ruins card night.

— G.

rationing_memo.title: OPERATIONS MEMO — GALLEY COPY, GREASE-STAINED
rationing_memo.body:
FROM: MERIDIAN DEEP ENERGY, LOGISTICS
TO: ALL SALTLINE GALLEY STATIONS
RE: PROVISIONING ADJUSTMENT — EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY

Standing food resupply is reduced 40% for the remainder of the quarter. Galley staff will implement portion scheduling per the attached table.

This adjustment is logistical in nature. Crews with questions should direct them to their section leads, who have been instructed not to answer them.

NOTE IN PEN, UNDERLINED TWICE: 'reduced for WHAT. we are 900 miles from anywhere. where does 40% of our food GO'

quiet_rig_note.title: TALLY BOOK PAGE — REC ROOM, UNDER THE DARTBOARD
quiet_rig_note.body:
Werner swears the crew on the end rig signed papers thick as a fist. Says his cousin worked the supply run — they offload at night, nobody on deck, crane does it all.

Kristjan asked the company man straight out at the safety brief: what's it called, the end platform. Man smiled and said 'that's a processing terminus.' Processing what? Smiled again.

We've started calling it the Quiet Rig. Feels wrong to even write it down.

Anyway. Darts Thursday. Werner owes me a bottle.

breaker_log.title: MAINTENANCE LOG — BREAKER ROOM 4-A
breaker_log.body:
ELECTRICAL MAINTENANCE — RUNNING LOG

04TH — Topside floodlight circuit tripping under load. Suspect corroded feed line in the stairwell corridor run. Flagged for splice.

09TH — Splice postponed. Cable stock requisition DENIED, all spool inventory redirected 'down the line.' Down the line. Everything goes down the line now.

11TH — Found scorch marks on the corridor run. Arc fault. Killed the whole circuit at the master rather than risk a fire. Topside's dark until we get spool stock.

If you need the deck lights: splice the corridor gap FIRST, then close the master here. In that order, unless you enjoy arc flash.

— E.V., chief electrician

machine_shop_sign.title: NOTICE — MACHINE SHOP WINDOW
machine_shop_sign.body:
MACHINE SHOP SEALED BY ORDER OF OIM

Hot-work permits suspended pending investigation of unauthorized fabrication activity.

Beneath the notice, scratched into the paint:

'they know about the raft'

lookout_note.title: WEATHERED NOTEBOOK — LOOKOUT POINT
lookout_note.body:
Best view on the whole line, and nobody comes up here but me and the gulls.

You can see all seven from the mast on a clear day. Ours, then the line of them, smaller and smaller, all the way out to the end one. The bridges look like stitches. Like somebody sewed the sea shut.

Funny thing I noticed and can't stop noticing: the bridges get worse the farther out you look. Every big storm they patch ours first. Like the far end doesn't matter.

Or like they know something's going to happen to it anyway.

pump_room_tag.title: LAMINATED TAG — FLOODED PUMP ROOM
pump_room_tag.body:
PUMP ROOM 1-C — LOCKOUT/TAGOUT

DO NOT RESTART. Bilge pumps offline for impeller service.

Dated the 11th. The month is smeared.

The tag is attached to a valve wheel below the waterline now. Whoever meant to come back to this never did.

coffee_note.title: NAPKIN UNDER A FULL COFFEE CUP — GALLEY
coffee_note.body:
In pencil, casual handwriting:

'Osk — night shift owes you for covering. Coffee's fresh, made a whole pot at 0330. Drink it while it's hot.

Back in five.'

The cup is full. The pot is full.

Everything here is exactly five minutes before something.

roof_mark.title: CHALK TALLY — BUNKHOUSE ROOF
roof_mark.body:
Someone came up here often. A wind-worn chalk tally on the roof plate, grouped in fives — thirty-one marks, then a gap, then four more drawn heavier, gouged in.

Beside it, a chalk sketch: the horizon line, and above it a shape with wide flat wings. Underneath, three words, gone over twice:

IT COMES BACK.

shrine_note.title: KELP-WRAPPED NOTE — CABIN B-03
shrine_note.body:
They said burn it. I couldn't.

It's not rot. It's not algae. You hold a frond up at night and it holds light INSIDE it, steady as a pilot lamp. Nothing that means harm keeps a light like that.

I've been leaving the porthole cracked. If the glow wants in, I want to know what it wants.

— O.

cabin_b05_scrawl.title: SCRAWL ON THE WALL — CABIN B-05
cabin_b05_scrawl.body:
Written in grease pencil, fast, the letters climbing the wall:

COUNTED 41 AT MUSTER. LAUNCHED WITH 40.

WHO STAYED?

toolpusher_log.title: TOOLPUSHER'S LOG — FINAL PAGE
toolpusher_log.body:
0400 — String's quiet. Not the quiet of a good hole. The quiet of something listening back up it.

0430 — Told Control we're shutting in. Nobody argued. Nobody EVER doesn't argue.

0600 — Company man wants it in writing. Fine. IN WRITING: the sea lit up under leg four and every gauge on this deck read zero at the same second. Pressure doesn't do that. Water doesn't do that.

Last entry.

medbay_note.title: SICK-BAY LEDGER
medbay_note.body:
Day 11 — Deckhand, R.: says the light off the water 'stays behind his eyes' after night watch. No fever. Pupils fine. Prescribed sleep he won't take.

Day 12 — Three more with the same words. THE SAME WORDS. Men who don't share a shift.

Day 13 — I looked tonight. It does stay. It isn't harmful. That's not the same as safe.

(The rest of the ledger is water-swollen and unreadable.)

comms_log.title: LAST TRANSMISSION LOG
comms_log.body:
TX 2241 — SALTLINE-1 to STANCHION: evac complete less one (1). Repeat, one crew unaccounted. Sea state 4. Bloom state — no code for it. Visual: the water is AWAKE.

RX 2244 — STANCHION: say again last?

TX 2247 — SALTLINE-1: ...

TX 2251 — SALTLINE-1: disregard. Going dark. Keep the lamps lit for us.

(Nothing further. The set's dial is still tuned.)

generator_tag.title: GENERATOR FAULT TAG
generator_tag.body:
OUT OF SERVICE — DO NOT CRANK

Fuel: contaminated (bio). Filters: fouled, green residue, GLOWS FAINT AT NIGHT.

If you need power, the topside floodlight circuit still takes a splice at Breaker 4-A. Cable's the hard part. Cable's always the hard part.

— maintenance, last shift

mooring_log.title: MOORING WATCH LOG — STATION SW
mooring_log.body:
WINDLASS 4-SW — WATCH ENTRIES

Day shift: chain wash-down complete, links 40-60 regreased. Tension nominal.

Night shift: tension spiked 0300, eased by 0340. Swell from the SW. Logged, not reported.

The last entry is the 14th, 0250: 'Something on the chain. Went to look.'

Nothing after that. The grease gun is still clipped to the rail.

fender_tag.title: INSPECTION TAG — BOAT LANDING
fender_tag.body:
FENDER PANEL 3 — QUARTERLY INSPECTION

Rubbing strips: 60% wear, replace next rotation. Tire fenders: serviceable.

Inspector's initials worn to a smudge of salt.

Stamped across the bottom in the company's blue ink: MERIDIAN DEEP ENERGY — SALTLINE PROJECT. The landing was due for service the week the ocean went quiet.

rigger_handbook.title: RIGGER'S HANDBOOK
rigger_handbook.body:
RIGGER'S HANDBOOK — SHOP COPY
Chained to the bench. Grease-thumbed, corners soft.

HOW THE BENCH WORKS
Press E at the bench to open it. Lay parts from your pack onto
the top — the bench shows what they want to become and what's
still missing. When a recipe is complete, hold WORK (or Space)
to hammer it real. Partial layouts are safe; take parts back
anytime. Some things must be seared here too, not just built.

————————————————————————————————
RECIPES

■ THROWING HOOK
   Needs: 1× Rope Coil + 1× Prybar
   Work: ~2s at the bench
   A heaving line with teeth. Takes back what the gyre holds.
   — Rope from the crane deck; prybar from the pump room.

■ PLANK WALKWAY
   Needs: 2× Driftwood Plank
   Work: ~2s at the bench
   A lashed plank section. Bridges a gap, extends a deck.
   — Two sound planks make a path where there wasn't one.

■ LEAN-TO
   Needs: 1× Canvas Tarp + 2× Driftwood Plank
   Work: ~3s at the bench
   Canvas over a driftwood frame. A pocket of warmth anywhere on the rig.
   — The sea gives back wood and canvas. Make a roof of them.

■ BARRICADE
   Needs: 1× Driftwood Plank + 2× Scrap Metal
   Work: ~3s at the bench
   Scrap plate on a wood brace. Waist-high, storm-solid.
   — Plate the gyre coughs up still remembers being a wall.

■ BLOOM LAMP
   Needs: 2× Kelp Bundle + 1× Scrap Metal
   Work: ~3s at the bench
   Bloom-kelp sealed in a scrap housing. Cold teal light, no power needed — and what walks at night honors it.
   — Kelp glows for weeks in a sealed housing. The crew knew.

■ DROP NET
   Needs: 2× Rope Coil + 1× Driftwood Plank
   Work: ~3s at the bench
   A weighted mesh on a winch line. Lower it off an edge, let the sea walk in, haul.
   — Set it before dusk — the night shift swims shallower.

■ SEARED GLOW WORM
   Needs: 1× Glow Worm
   Work: ~2s at the bench
   A minute on hot steel and the light goes out of it. What's left is honest meat.
   — Raw ones bite back on the way down. Sear it first.

————————————————————————————————
FISHING (a later hand, in pencil)
Rod's in the storeroom. Cast to open water [LMB], strike when
the float plunges, then reel the lulls and rest the surges —
if the strain bar tops out, the line parts. The drop net does
the patient version: build it AT A DECK EDGE, lower, walk away,
haul. Raw catch sears on the galley stove upstairs. Eat cooked.

A last note, pencilled in the margin:
"The gyre keeps giving it back. Rope, plank, plate, canvas.
 Whatever you lose to the water washes up by the third dawn.
 Build like the sea's on your side. It is."

anglers_notes.title: ANGLER'S NOTES
anglers_notes.body:
ANGLER'S NOTES — WET DECK COPY
A rigger's log of what the water gives, and when. Kept honest.

READ THE WATER: every cast tells you the conditions — the hour,
rig shadow or open water, storm or calm, worklight on the swell.
Match the fish to the water and the water stops being luck.

■ COPPER SPRAT   (rod+net)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: surface
   Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. The sea's small change.

■ LANTERN HERRING   (rod+net)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: surface
   The gateway catch. At night the shoal glows its own position away.

■ SLATE COD   (rod+net)
   When: day · Water: anywhere · Weather: storms help · Depth: mid
   Loves a gray sky — bites double under storm cloud. Heavy, honest meat.

■ LODESTONE BREAM   (rod)
   When: day · Water: open water · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Deep daylight water. Its magnetized bones spin a compass — catch enough, craft crude magnets, someday.

■ EMBER SNAPPER   (rod+net)
   When: day/dusk · Water: rig shadow · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Warm-bodied — crowds the rig's outfalls and warm steel. Fish the shadow of the deck.

■ CHIMEFISH   (rod+net)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: calm only · Depth: mid
   Calm seas only — they won't ring in weather. Worth more traded than eaten, someday.

■ DRUM CROAKER   (rod+net)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: STORMS ONLY · Depth: mid
   Storm fish, full stop. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes — then they bite like they mean it.

■ MIRRORJACK   (rod)
   When: dawn/dusk · Water: open water · Weather: any · Depth: surface
   A dawn and dusk feeder in open water — fast, chrome, furious on the line.

■ SILVER LADDER   (rod)
   When: dawn · Water: open water · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Dawn columns over open water — the shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar.

■ BARREL GROUPER   (rod)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: open water · Weather: storms help · Depth: deep
   Sears to a PRIME FILLET.
   The hardest fight on the rod. Deep open water; a storm stirs them up off the bottom. Feeds you for days.

■ SABLE HAKE   (rod+net)
   When: night · Water: rig shadow · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Drawn to worklight — power the floodlights, fish the glow.
   Rises to worklight after dark like moths with fins. Power the floodlights and fish the glow.

■ INKWELL SQUID   (rod+net)
   When: night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Drawn to worklight — power the floodlights, fish the glow.
   Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink — the ink's worth keeping too, someday.

■ THE LOOKER   (rod)
   When: night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Never kept. You'll understand at the rail.
   Any water, any hour, almost never. It is not kept. You'll understand at the rail.

■ GHOST SOLE   (rod+net)
   When: night · Water: rig shadow · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Drawn to worklight — power the floodlights, fish the glow.
   Near-invisible by day. Night water near a glow is where it shows itself.

■ GLASSPIKE   (rod)
   When: night · Water: open water · Weather: calm only · Depth: surface
   Clear still nights, open water — a pike you see through, found by the grit in its gut.

■ RIBBON EEL   (rod)
   When: night · Water: open water · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Sears to a PRIME FILLET.
   Deep dark water only. Comes up faintly crackling — the Bloom keeps strange batteries.

■ GUTTER PRAWN   (net)
   When: dawn/day/dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: mid
   Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few — the pens will want them, someday.

■ MILLER'S FLOUNDER   (net)
   When: day · Water: rig shadow · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Deck-plate camouflage, bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them by day.

■ STONE CRAB   (net)
   When: dusk/night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Walks into a soaked net, never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard — keep the pieces, someday.

■ FATHOM HALIBUT   (net)
   When: night · Water: anywhere · Weather: any · Depth: deep
   Sears to a PRIME FILLET.
   Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up, and the winch knows about it. Feeds a week.

————————————————————————————————
Margins, later hand: "The net gathers, the rod hunts. The stove
makes it a meal. Raw will turn on you — a minute on hot steel won't."

KEEPING IT: raw turns in ~4 hours. HANG it on a marked line (raw
→ rotten, cooked → DRIED, keeps forever) or STOW it in the galley
fridge (always fresh). The sea below the swell is swimmable now —
cold, patrolled, and past ~13m down, not yours. Dock ladder's the
way back up.

osk_watch_slate.title: Night Watch Slate
osk_watch_slate.body:
Grease pencil on a scratched watch slate, half wiped for the next shift.

0210 — quiet. 0245 — quiet. 0310 —

it isn't in the water. the water is IN it. i put the lamp on it and it didn't run and it didn't come, it just — turned, the way you turn when someone says your name.

Henrik thinks I spook. I don't spook. I've watched this sea eleven years. This is the first time it's ever watched back.

— O.

osk_last_note.title: Folded Note, Weighted With a Shell
osk_last_note.body:
Whoever finds this: don't wait for me at the boats. I'm not going.

It isn't sickness and it isn't fear. R. had the words wrong in the sick-bay — it doesn't stay behind your eyes. It stays in front. Once you've seen the sea lit from the inside you can't want the dark back.

They'll say I stayed. I didn't stay. I'm going the other way down the line, toward the light, while the rest of you row toward the shore that turned its back on us.

Keep the lamps lit. Not for me. For whoever the machine spits back up.

— Osk

sat_dive_log.title: Saturation Log — Laminated Card
sat_dive_log.body:
BELL RUN 14 — SAT DAY 09 OF 16
Diver at storage depth. DO NOT DECOMPRESS OUTSIDE SCHEDULE.

In pen, fast, not the same hand as the printed log:

'muster called. we can't bring the bell up in time — you'd die on the way. putting you in the pod. it'll bring you up slow and safe, six days, no matter what happens up here. i'm sorry. i'm so sorry. we'll leave a lamp on.
— don't be angry we left. be alive.'

chess_note.title: Score Card Under a Chess Piece
chess_note.body:
Werner is up 3 games to 2. The board is mid-game, white to move, a scrap of card under the white king in Kristjan's blocky print:

'W — if I don't make it back for this, mate finishes in four moves and you know it. Don't you dare reset the board. Some of us are coming back to win properly.
— K.'

White never moved.

raft_plan.title: Drafting-Table Sketch
raft_plan.body:
Through the shop glass: a raft, drawn careful and to scale, hull numbers worked out twice. Oil drums for float, deck plate for a keel, a mast stepped from a derrick pipe. Provisions list in the corner — that's where the missing 40% of the food went, a can at a time, into a locker under the bench.

Across the whole sheet, later, in a shaking hand:
'won't matter. the sea turns everything back. Osk was right. there's no west anymore. there's only down the line.'

The raft is three planks from finished. It will always be three planks from finished.

henrik_photo.title: Photograph Taped Inside a Bunk
henrik_photo.body:
Two boys on a stony beach, squinting into a grey sun, holding up a fish too small to keep. On the back, a woman's round handwriting:

'They caught it themselves. Told everyone at school their dad's a deep-sea man. Come home and be one on land for a while. — M.'

Henrik made the boats. The photo didn't. He'll have gone over the rail counting the days he had left — three weeks, he kept writing. Three weeks.

company_man_memo.title: Sealed Directive — Eyes Only
company_man_memo.body:
MERIDIAN DEEP ENERGY — PROJECT SALTLINE
RE: TERMINUS YIELD — CONTAINMENT POSTURE

The bioluminescent yield at Platform 7 exceeds projection by an order of magnitude and is no longer responding to the inhibitor feed. Recommend we cease characterizing it as a contaminant. It is the product. It was always the product.

Do NOT advise the line crews. Panic reduces output. Maintain the provisioning schedule; the yield feeds on the organic input and we require it to keep feeding.

Handwritten across the seal, pressed hard enough to tear:
'we were the feed. all of us. 900 miles out so no one would hear the line go quiet.'

ev_last_splice.title: Note Pinned to the Breaker Panel
ev_last_splice.body:
If you're reading this, you found the splice notes and you got the topside lights up. Good. That means the rig's got someone in it again.

I couldn't get us cable. They took every spool down the line. So I'm leaving you what I couldn't finish and one piece of advice a chief owes a stranger: the crab won't cross a lamp. Not because it's scared. Because it was made polite. Somebody down the line built it that way, and I don't like to think about who, or why they needed a thing that big kept polite.

Keep the lamps lit. It's the whole job now.

— E.V.

bottle_note.title: Note in a Bottle
bottle_note.body:
Salt-swollen, corked with candle wax. The current brought it in against the dock the way the current brings everything.

— no header, just a hand —

if you're reading this you're on one of the rigs and you're alive and that already makes you rare. we launched from Rig 6 and the sea won't let the boats go west. it turns us. every boat. back toward the line.

maybe that's cruelty. maybe it's the only kindness left — it doesn't want us to drown out there alone. we're rowing back. tell whoever's on 4 to keep a lamp in the window.

we'll be a few days. everything out here is a few days.
